evidence: InMemoryOrderRepository.ts and InMemoryProductRepository.ts both store data as a Map of snapshots, call toSnapshot() on save and restore() on read, so the snapshot approach is applied the same way in both.

OrderController.ts only calls this.useCases.* (placeOrder, advanceOrder, cancelOrder, getOrder, listOrders). StockController.ts only calls listStockLevels.execute(). Neither touches a repository directly.

requestParsers.ts: parseStatusQuery reuses the domain's isOrderStatus instead of keeping its own list of statuses. parsePlaceOrderBody says it checks only the body's shape and that 'business rules are enforced by the domain'.
errorHandler.ts: statusFor(DomainError) is the only place that maps domain errors to HTTP status codes.
catalogueSeed.ts: seedCatalogue(products: ProductRepository) goes through the repository abstraction and Product.create rather than writing to the storage directly.
app.ts: createApp() is the only composition root, and server.ts only calls createApp().listen.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The files form one cohesive concern: they are the adapters around the core plus its composition root. That covers persistence (the two in-memory repositories), system ports (SystemClock, UuidIdGenerator), the HTTP delivery code (OrderController, StockController, requestParsers, errorHandler), seed data (catalogueSeed), and wiring and startup (app.ts, server.ts). Persistence and HTTP code share one module, but every file adapts the core to the outside world, and app.ts brings them together on purpose, so they are not unrelated concerns. The module uses its abstractions consistently. Both repositories store snapshots and rebuild entities with restore. Controllers only call use cases. The seed goes through ProductRepository and Product.create. Each rule lives in one place. Status checks reuse isOrderStatus from the domain. requestParsers checks only the request's shape and leaves business rules to the domain. Mapping errors to HTTP status codes happens only in errorHandler. I found no duplicated invariant and no bypass of an abstraction.
